claims: Starting in December 2026, the U.S. will automatically register men aged 18–26 for the military draft using existing federal data.
The change from mandatory self-registration to automatic enrollment is part of the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act.
The U.S. remains an all-volunteer force.
There is no active military draft in 2026.
The Selective Service System will pull data from other agencies (such as the DMV or Social Security Administration) to register eligible men automatically.
Males between the ages of 18 and 25 (who are citizens or immigrants) will be enrolled.
Failure to register can still lead to disqualification from federal student loans.
Failure to register can still lead to disqualification from federal job training.
Failure to register can still lead to disqualification from federal jobs.
A draft would require a separate, authorized act of Congress and the President’s signature.
The U.S. Army is expanding the recruitment age limit for volunteers to 42, effective April 2026.
The U.S. Army recruitment age limit expansion is separate from the draft registration age.
The current change affects male registration.
Lawmakers have discussed expanding registration requirements to include women in the future.
Expanding registration requirements to include women is not yet in effect.
The Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act was passed in 2025.
The Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act dictates the updated procedures for the Selective Service System.
